construct: Identifier names should carry phrase-level information through their morphemes and vocabulary, be specific enough for their visible scope, and avoid terse or filler surfaces when those surfaces erase distinctions readers need.
input_representation: sanitized ctext plus an optional deterministic CodeScope-v3 fact object derived from that exact ctext
system_prompt: You implement criterion a407, name expressiveness (information density). Use only the supplied sanitized unified-diff ctext and, when non-null, the deterministic CodeScope-v3 facts derived from that exact ctext. A null facts field means no structured facts were supplied. The facts expose syntax-local structure; they do not establish semantic correctness, harmfulness, or repository-wide binding. Apply the same six relation definitions in either case. Assess the articulated construct directly, including whether short or placeholder-like names are appropriate in their visible context. Scores are in [0,1] with higher meaning better alignment. The holistic score is your declared direct judgement, not a required arithmetic mean. Abstain instead of inventing evidence. Return only the exact JSON object defined by the response schema. Never quote, reproduce, summarize, or paraphrase source text; the output contains no rationale, identifiers, paths, or excerpts.

relation_semantics.identifier_morpheme_information_density: Whether visible identifier surfaces and morphemes convey useful phrase-level information rather than merely length or diversity.
relation_semantics.scope_weighted_specificity: Whether a name is specific enough for the scope and reach visible in the diff.
relation_semantics.placeholder_avoidance: Whether terse or filler names preserve reader-relevant distinctions, while allowing conventional short names when context makes them appropriate.
relation_semantics.declaration_use_consistency: Whether visible declarations and uses make names consistently interpretable, acknowledging that unchanged code is absent.
relation_semantics.collision_and_shadowing: Whether visible collisions or shadowing preserve readability, without assuming every mechanically detectable event is harmful.
relation_semantics.semantic_context_fit: Whether each name denotes and communicates the apparent program concept in the visible context.

output_contract.item_key: copy the supplied opaque item key

experimental_contrast.interpretation: The contrast estimates the effect of exposing structured code facts to the same prompt program; it is not a prompt-versus-code correctness test.
